learningObjective: Understand CUDA constant memory: 64 KB module-scope, per-SM constant cache, warp-broadcast on uniform access.

canonicalClaims.claim: CUDA `__constant__` memory is a 64 KB per-module region cached in a dedicated per-SM constant cache; it is optimized for warp-uniform reads (broadcast in one access) and is populated from host via `cudaMemcpyToSymbol` before kernel launch.
nonImplications: Does not imply non-uniform reads are free.
Does not imply constant memory is device-writable during kernel execution.

misconceptions.claim: Constant memory is unlimited in size.
Constant memory is writable from the device kernel.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Only host writes via cudaMemcpyToSymbol; device sees it as read-only.

misconceptions.claim: Constant memory is always faster than shared memory.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Only for warp-uniform reads; non-uniform serializes.

implementationFacts: `__constant__ float table[N];` at file scope; `cudaMemcpyToSymbol(table, ...)` on host.
Broadcast: warp-uniform reads serve in one access.
